_readme: SIMULATOR FIXTURES, NOT GAME CONTENT. Synthetic enemies for Tooling/BalanceSim's PvE mode, so the roster can be measured against PvE-shaped fights. They are not roster beasts, no game code reads this file, and nothing here is a design decision about real encounters. Two sets. (1) The default, generated set: EnemyTypes is a pool of enemy types and Shapes the encounter shapes (solo, elite, squad, horde); the simulator draws --compositions random compositions per shape from its Variants (each slot draws a count in [Min, Max], then each unit's type uniformly from Types), keeps a draw only if its summed type Threat is inside ThreatBudget and it has at least MinDistinctTypes types, and assigns elements per composition by a random scheme (one element for the whole team, one per type, one per unit, or none), dealt from a shuffled deck of the ten elements. (2) FixedEncounters: the three hand-authored encounters of earlier runs (--encounter-set fixed), with per-group Count and Elements (cycled over the group). BaseStats are max-level values scaled by the roster growth curve named in GrowthCurveId (as a beast's are); the simulator then calibrates one difficulty multiplier per shape (or fixed encounter), level and kit mode, so only the ratios inside a stat line, and between the types that share a shape, matter. Threat is a hand-set estimate in 'standard enemy = 2' units that only keeps a shape's compositions comparably hard; the report lists each composition's clear rate at the shape's calibrated difficulty so the estimate can be checked. Speeds sit in a narrow 95-105 band, comparable to the planned roster band. MoveRange sits inside the roster's own band (beasts move 2-5): BattleTurnExecutor makes a partial approach, so no enemy needs board-spanning movement to engage. CritChance is a percent (0-100), exempt from the growth curve and from the difficulty multiplier. The loader requires MoveRange >= 1, CritChance 0-100 and at least one SingleTarget skill. Stance is a CombatStance name (missing = Vanguard); a Ranged enemy needs a SingleTarget skill with Range >= 2 (a Ranged unit never walks into melee). StatusResist (0-100, missing = 0) is BattleUnit.StatusResist: the percent knocked off the chance of every hostile non-damage effect aimed at the enemy; the bosses (giant, champion, colossus) carry 50. Footprint is a UnitFootprint name (missing = Single, one tile): the giant and the colossus are Hex7 (seven tiles, the boss size), the champion Triangle (three tiles, the mini-boss size); see docs/design/battle-system.md, 'Unit footprints'. Every range to or from a large enemy is measured between nearest tiles, so the Hex7 bosses' ranges are authored one lower than their one-tile values were (gaze 2, quake and roar 1) to keep their reach from the centre unchanged; a large caster's AreaBurst is the union of the discs around its tiles (Range 1 from a Hex7 is the radius-2 disc around its centre). The loader packs every shape's worst case (each slot at Max, its largest type) and every fixed encounter into the enemy zone the way a battle does, and refuses what does not fit: a Hex7 enemy never fits a Small arena. Optional per-skill fields, all inert when missing: HitCount (damage hits, default 1), ExecuteBonusPercent (default 0), InitialCooldown (-1 = the ordinary cooldown; 0 fires on the first turn), MaxUsesPerBattle (0 = unlimited) and Effects, a list of further SkillEffects after the damage effect ({ Type, Status, Stat, Magnitude, DurationTurns, Chance, MaxStacks, IsPercent, HitCount, ExecuteBonusPercent }; Type and Status are SkillEffectType / StatusType names). No fixture uses them yet. Targeting is a SkillTargetingCriterion name (missing = Distance, i.e. nearest; Random is refused so battles never draw targets from the rng), with optional TargetingOrder (missing = Lowest) and TargetingStat (missing = HP, only read by Stat, which compares the stat block's maximum). CurrentHp compares the HP a beast has left, so CurrentHp/Lowest is 'pick off the weakest'. Skill Power is a percent of the attacking stat (DamageFormula: Power / 100 * A * A / (A + D)); the powers were rescaled from the old level-term formula so an average hit takes the same share of HP at level 50. See Tooling/BalanceSim/README.md.

Shapes.Description: One giant: huge HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn and a periodic area slam in both. Compositions differ only in the giant's element.
A boss with an escort: one giant and two standard enemies, or two champions (mini-bosses) and one or two standard enemies.
Four to six standard enemies of at least three types: melee tanks, hunters, archers, casters and shamans.

Sixteen to twenty-four enemies: mostly swarm (tiny melee: swarmlings bite, physical; stinglings sting, special; one skill each, since every hit deals at least the damage floor), with a few archers and casters behind them.

FixedEncounters.Description: One huge enemy: very high HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn, and a periodic area slam. Vanguard, always hitting the nearest beast. Elementless by default so the boss measures stat lines; use --enemy-element for an elemental variant.

Twenty-four small enemies with low HP and weak melee: half bite (Physical), half sting (Special), so neither defence is favoured. Biters are Vanguard and bite the nearest beast; stingers are Skirmishers that go for the beast with the least HP left and dart back after stinging. Elements cycle through all ten. Move 4 for every unit: the Large board's zones are 8 apart, so the swarm closes over two turns by partial approach.

Six mid-size enemies: three fast Physical melee hunters in front (Vanguard, nearest beast), three Special casters behind them at range 3 (Ranged, the beast with the least HP left). Six different elements.
